Native registration table

Research date: 30 October 2026. Dump: research/dumps/1158.16-a.bin, image base 0x140000000, SizeOfImage 0x5b45200. Dumps must never be committed (see .gitignore).

Image layout

Two executable sections:

  • .text at 0x1000, size 0x2479400. Ordinary code, including every native handler.
  • A second .text at 0x5123000, size 0xa22200. Arxan-obfuscated code. Most native registration sites reside here.

The .retplne and .voltbl sections are present, which identifies the build as clang/LLVM-compiled. The image was not relocated under Wine and loaded at its preferred base.

Registration function

register(table, hash, handler) is at RVA 0x920d70, with rcx holding the table, rdx the hash and r8 the handler. It has 25 direct callers, all of them BUILTIN natives, for example the block at 0x922f20. The remaining registration is inlined or obfuscated in the second .text.

The table is at RVA 0x3ED4C20, established from lea rsi, [rip+0x35b1cf4] at 0x922f25. It consists of 256 plain bucket pointers indexed by hash & 0xff.

Node layout (0x100 bytes, maximum 7 entries):

Offset Content
+0x00/+0x04 Next pointer low and high, each XORed with ((u32)node ^ dword[+0x08])
+0x10 + i*8 Handler i (plain pointer)
+0x48 Count, XORed with dword[+0x4c] and (u32)(node+0x48)
+0x54 + i*16 Hash low and high, each XORed with ((u32)(node+0x54+i*16) ^ dword[+0x5c+i*16])
+0xc8 + i*8 Zero at registration (cache slot)

The keys originate from an LCG (x*0x343fd + 0x269ec3) stored at RVA 0x286a96c. The design matches Legacy.

tools/dump/openv-natives.exe walks the table in a live process:

  • 6748 natives in 1076 nodes, with a maximum chain length of 6.
  • 6524 unique handlers, because some natives share a stub.

Hash randomisation

Only 270 of 6748 table hashes match the alloc8or nativedb "universal" hashes:

  • mostly BUILTIN;
  • plus natives first added in builds approximately 2944 to 3889.

The remaining 96 percent are randomised for this build, so a crossmap is required.

Context ABI (identical to Legacy)

handler(ctx):

  • [ctx+0x00] is the return-value pointer.
  • [ctx+0x10] is the argument array, 8 bytes per argument.

Floats are read with movss [args + i*8].

Crossmap feasibility: signals found

  1. Handler address order approximates nativedb order.
    • Sorted by handler address, 264 of 269 anchor steps increase in nativedb order.
    • Of the longest increasing anchor chain (233 anchors, 232 gaps), 185 gaps have exactly equal sizes on both sides, which fixes approximately 2026 natives plus the anchors by position alone.
    • A few large mismatches (plus or minus 1290) appear to be whole namespaces ordered differently. The next step is per-namespace block alignment.
  2. Handler signatures. 6496 of 6524 handlers begin with an Arxan jmp chain.
    • research/trace.py follows the jumps and tracks the context and argument registers.
    • It recovers the exact parameter count for 224 of 270 anchors (83 percent).
    • The misses are zero-argument readings caused by deeper obfuscation (spilled argument pointers, indirect jumps).
  3. Not yet used: return-type writes ([ctx] usage, xmm versus integer), the Vector3 return pattern, and call targets shared with known handlers.

Next steps

  • Align namespace blocks (dynamic programming or Needleman-Wunsch), scored by parameter count and return kind, then measure how many natives are uniquely resolved.
  • Improve the tracer for stack spills, push/ret and lea-based jumps.
  • Validate the result in game: call approximately 20 resolved natives from a test ASI and check the behaviour.
  • Legal: nativedb-data has no LICENSE file. Use only names, hashes and signatures (facts), never comments. Ask the maintainer before publishing generated headers.
